title: The light of the world (John 8:12)
hookLine: whoever follows me walks not in darkness
tomorrow: The truth shall make you free

lines: THE EASTER VIGIL IN THE DARK.
cards: The Easter Vigil begins in the dark. The church is black. A single fire is lit outside, and from it one tall candle.
A deacon carries it in and stops three times, lifting it and singing the same short phrase: the light of Christ.
People light their small candles from it, and the light moves back through the church, hand to hand, until the whole building glows.
What the candle proclaims goes back to one sentence Jesus spoke in the middle of an old feast of lamps. We're still at the feast of Tabernacles.

teach.h: GOLDEN LAMPS IN THE TEMPLE COURT.
teach.b: The feast had water, and it also had light. The Jewish sources describe great golden lampstands set up in the temple courts, so tall that young priests climbed ladders to fill them with oil.
The wicks were made from the priests' worn-out garments. The old account says there wasn't a courtyard in Jerusalem that didn't shine with their light, and men danced with torches through the night.

Jesus is teaching in the treasury, John says, right by that court. And he says, in the Douay-Rheims: "I am the light of the world: he that followeth me, walketh not in darkness, but shall have the light of life."
It's the second great I am. Bread is what you need every day; light is what lets you see everything else. Notice the promise.
He doesn't say there will be no darkness. He says the one who follows will not walk in it.

teach.h: NOT NO DARK: NOT WALKING IN IT.
teach.b: Following is a walking word: a lamp held up ahead on a dark road.
You still have to walk, but you can see where to put your feet.
We heard this light at the start of the Gospel: the light shineth in darkness. In Matthew, Jesus turns it around: you are the light of the world.
The Church holds both together: Christ is the light, and those who follow him carry it. That's the Easter Vigil in one gesture: one candle, then every hand passing the flame along.

how: At the Easter Vigil Catholics light the paschal candle from a new fire and pass its flame to candles throughout the church, as the deacon sings "the light of Christ" three times.

games.q: you're teaching in the temple during a feast when great lamps light the whole city at night. what do you say?
o: these lamps remind us of God's glory.
I am the light of the world.
these lamps will one day go out.
games.why: "I am the light of the world: he that followeth me, walketh not in darkness." he speaks in the treasury, by the court where the lamps stood.

practice: Stand by a window or a lamp, or step outside into daylight, and walk slowly toward the light, feeling each step land. Notice how light changes what you see: edges, colors, faces, your own hands.
If you pray, hold the line, he that followeth me walketh not in darkness; if not, just walk and notice the light.
